claim: The reference channel is a coarse per-(fragment_a,fragment_b)-pair lookup: exactly 539 distinct pairs, 0 pairs carrying more than one reference value, with bimodal-by-bond-class error (C-H bias +5.1029, C-C bias -3.3033).
value_found: 539 distinct ordered (fragment_a_smiles, fragment_b_smiles) pairs among 543 benchmark rows; 0 pairs with >1 distinct reference_estimate_bde_kcal_mol (max-min = 0.0 for every pair); unordered-pair key gives the same 539 and 0; 4 pairs are duplicated across cis/trans parents (n=2 each) and each duplicate still carries one single shared reference value (93.2/93.2, 91.4/91.4, 104.7/104.7, 132.5/132.5). C-H bias = +5.102914 (n=302, RDKit radical-centre bond_class == 'C-H'); C-C bias = -3.303333 (n=240, bond_class == 'C-C'); the single H-O observation (bond_observation_0181, exp=83.1, ref=83.3, err=+0.2) is the 1 remaining row of 543. Under the alternative 'any H-containing fragment' grouping the C-H bias is +5.086733 (n=303) and C-C is -3.303333 (n=240), so both labelings agree to within the effect of that one H-O row.
unit: individual benchmark observation (543 rows) grouped by bond observation (each row = one bond observation; 539 unique ordered fragment pairs); per-bond-class means of (reference_estimate - experimental_bde)
method: Independent inline python3 (heredoc) scripts, NOT the original workstream script: pandas.read_csv(data/normalized_views/experimental_benchmark.tsv, sep='\t'); groupby(['fragment_a_smiles','fragment_b_smiles'])['reference_estimate_bde_kcal_mol'].nunique() and .agg(['max','min']); bond classes recomputed from scratch via RDKit Chem.MolFromSmiles + GetNumRadicalElectrons + element-priority sort (C,H,N,O,S,P,F,Cl,Br,I); groupby('bond_class').mean(ref - exp). Cross-checked the same 543 rows by reading data/source_data/experimental_source_tables.xlsx directly with openpyxl (load_workbook read_only/data_only, Sheet_001), joined one-to-one on (Molecule, Radical 1, Radical 2): max|tsv - xlsx| = 0.0 for both the reference and observed columns. DB check: pandas.read_csv(data/source_data/bde_db_full.csv.gz) groupby(['fragment1','fragment2'])['bde'].nunique(). See inline commands; outputs: 290 distinct reference values for 543 rows (max 1 per pair).
notes: Every element of the claim reproduces exactly at the stated precision. (1) 539/0: unique pair count is 539 for both ordered and unordered keys, and no pair has >1 distinct reference value (535 pairs appear once, 4 twice; the 4 doubled pairs are cis/trans parent stereoisomers of the same fragment pair and share one identical reference value, e.g. ref=93.2 for both C/C=C/C(C)C and C/C=C\C(C)C). (2) Bias: +5.102914 (claim +5.1029) and -3.303333 (claim -3.3033) reproduce to 4 dp using RDKit radical-centre bond classes; the 3rd 'class' is a single H-O row (err +0.2) not mentioned in the claim. Under a crude 'fragment == [H]' grouping the C-H value becomes +5.086733 (n=303, includes the H-O row), still equal to the claim at the quoted precision only if the RDKit-style classes are used - i.e. the claim is self-consistent with the common.bond_class labeler. (3) 'Bimodal' is supported soft evidence, not a sharp two-peak density: a 2-component GMM on the 542 C-H/C-C errors gives means -2.55/+4.60, weights 0.45/0.55, delta-BIC = +15.2 versus 1 component (positive = 1-component preferred; driven by unequal class sizes and within-class spread), while class separation is very strong (Welch t=18.23, p=3e-55; point-biserial r=0.630) and only 8.3% of C-H errors fall inside the C-C IQR. (4) Confound: reference error correlates with experimental BDE globally (r=0.147, p=6e-4) and within C-C (r=0.267, p=3e-5), so 'bimodal by bond class' is partly a bond-strength/bond-class confound, but that is a caveat on interpretation, not a numeric failure. (5) Out-of-benchmark probe: only 331/543 benchmark pairs occur in bde_db_full.csv.gz, and the benchmark reference value does not match the DB per-pair median there (only 1/331 within 0.05 kcal/mol), so the reference channel is a benchmark-level lookup, not a DB-derived one; note bde_db_full.csv.gz itself is NOT pair-unique (23/290641 pairs have >1 bde), so the 'per-pair lookup' property belongs to the benchmark reference channel, not to the quantum DB. (6) The task template mentions a two-method check (claim 5) and a naive pooled-variance ~165 number (claim 11); neither is a component of claim 12, so neither applies here.
